subject: physics

moments.title: Schrödinger in the Alps
moments.body: Schrödinger, 38, takes Christmas holiday in the Alps with an unidentified woman (not his wife). Inspired by de Broglie's matter waves, he derives a wave equation for the electron. In weeks he solves hydrogen, harmonic oscillator, and rotor.
moments.takeaway: The most important equation in chemistry is derived during a mountain affair.

moments.title: Born's probability interpretation
moments.body: Born proposes that |psi|^2 gives the probability density of finding a particle. The wave function is not a real wave but a probability amplitude. Einstein objects: 'God does not play dice.' Born wins the 1954 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: The wave function is a probability — not a physical wave.

moments.title: Dirac unifies quantum and relativity
moments.body: Dirac, 25, writes a relativistic wave equation for the electron. The solutions include both electrons and a mysterious 'antiparticle' with the same mass but opposite charge. Four years later Anderson finds the positron in cloud-chamber photographs.
moments.takeaway: Mathematics predicts antimatter before anyone observes it.

moments.title: Schrödinger's cat
moments.body: Schrödinger devises a thought experiment in which a cat is sealed in a box with a radioactive trigger. Until observation, the cat is in a superposition of alive and dead. He intends this as a reductio ad absurdum of the Copenhagen interpretation. It becomes the most famous illustration of quantum weirdness.

quote.text: I don't like it, and I'm sorry I ever had anything to do with it.

moments.takeaway: The inventor of the wave equation comes to dislike his own creation.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: The Schrödinger equation underlies all of quantum chemistry. Density functional theory computes molecular structures for millions of molecules. Quantum chemistry is central to drug discovery and materials design.
now.open_questions: Is wave function collapse a real physical process?

reflection: Schrödinger built the equation; he disliked the interpretation. Why are some scientists alienated by the consequences of their own work?
